data.narrative:
SambaNova Systems, a Series A chip design company founded by Rodrigo Liang, Kunle Olukotun, and Christopher Ré, is valued at $11.0B post-money following $1.1B in total capital raised. Valuation analysis triangulates across a universe of 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage comparables, including Rebellions ($2.3B Series A), d-Matrix ($2.0B Series A), and Positron AI ($1.0B Series B).

Two methods prove applicable. Stage-progression anchored to the $11.0B last post-money round and applying a typical 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier yields $22.0B. Peer-median valuation across the 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces $2.0B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median 18.4x across the three public tickers) cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue.

The triangulated range spans $1.7B (low) to $25.3B (high), with a median of $12.0B. The substantial dispersion reflects tension between the target's last institutional valuation and peer trading multiples. Key uncertainties include the timing and magnitude of next-stage funding, competitive positioning relative to the identified peer set, and revenue trajectory assumptions necessary to anchor public-market comparables.
